not_exported.detail: Fleet's built-in skills (presentation-builder, svg-builder, mermaid-diagram-builder, generate-skill, fleet-guide and others) ship with Fleet's runtime. The exported agent doesn't have them.

warnings: MCP server `weather` (https://weather.example.com/mcp) needs headers export can't set up: X-API-Key. Add them to tools/mcp yourself before you deploy.
Approvals: Fleet has approval rules for tools export didn't carry over: deleted_tool
left_behind: Conversations: past threads stay in Fleet. The deployment starts with none.
Credentials: saved logins don't carry over. Each user signs in again the first time a tool needs it.
Traces: the deployment traces to a new LangSmith project. Past traces stay in the Fleet agent's project.
notes: Connections: the agent uses your existing `notion` connection for https://mcp.notion.com/mcp.

connections.summary: The agent owns this connection to https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp, and a connection the agent owns can only be created once the deployment exists, so the server is commented out in `tools/mcp.py`.
steps: Set `ACME_2_TOKEN` to the token (without `Bearer `) and run `mda connections create acme-2 --secret-from-env ACME_2_TOKEN`

connections.summary: The agent signs in to https://mcp.github.example/mcp with each user's own account. `mda deploy` creates this connection through the server's OAuth discovery, and each user signs in the first time a tool needs it.

after_first_deploy: acme-2: set `ACME_2_TOKEN` to the token (without `Bearer `) and run `mda connections create acme-2 --secret-from-env ACME_2_TOKEN`
Then uncomment those servers in tools/mcp and run `mda deploy` again
memory: `memory.py` gives the agent its own memory in `memories/agent/`. It starts empty, and the agent adds to it as it learns.
